models.author: Tudor Beloiu
models.description: This model is designed to detect and classify traffic light states (Red, Green, Yellow) in real-time. It was trained using a custom dataset from Kaggle using the YOLOv8 architecture. You can find the full source code on my github repository: https://github.com/tudorbeloiu/TrafficLights

instances.overview: A CNN trained from scratch to classify traffic light colors (red, yellow, green) as an accessibility tool for colorblind drivers. YOLOv8 (pretrained on COCO) handles detection — it locates the traffic light in a full street image and crops it. The crop is then passed to the custom CNN for color classification. Yellow lights are heavily prioritized in training (recall 0.98) since missing a yellow is more dangerous than a false positive.
instances.usage:
from PIL import Image
import torchvision.transforms as transforms
import torch

transform = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize((64, 64)),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
])

img = Image.open("traffic_light_crop.jpg").convert("RGB")
x = transform(img).unsqueeze(0)  # shape: (1, 3, 64, 64)

model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    output = model(x)
    pred = torch.argmax(output, dim=1).item()

labels = {0: "green", 1: "red", 2: "yellow"}
print(labels[pred])

models.subtitle: Traffic light color classifier for colorblind drivers — custom CNN + YOLOv8 detection pipeline

models.description:
Arachnom is a 1.5B parameter code and reasoning model created by David Woodayan from scratch. It specializes in Python, programming, web development (HTML/CSS/JS), and step-by-step logical reasoning using chain-of-thought tags. 
Trained on competitive programming problems, olympiad-level math, and web development
datasets over 2 epochs. Designed to be lightweight,
fast, and deployable on a single consumer GPU. Base Model: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B
